rubric.item: SPEC-02 correctness (per recorded Q-2 deviation: band claim, not exit 0)

findings.issue: The test is named 'all-TAG 3-seat cash play passes --check-styles over 100,000 hands', but after the Q-2 deviation it does not assert that --check-styles passes; the documented run exits 1 (one-action rule on preflop-limpers). The name overstates what is checked.
findings.evidence: No assertion on `code`; docs/advice/range-model.md table records '3 seats, 100,000 hands, after | exit 1'. The comment at lines 8-9 explains the gap, but the name, which the spec uses as the verification id, does not.
findings.fix: Either keep the name for verification-id stability (and leave the comment as is), or rename it to e.g. 'all-TAG 3-seat cash aggression is inside the TAG band over 100,000 hands' and update the SPEC-02 verification id at the same time. Also worth doing when the rare-spot follow-up lands: restore the exit-0 assertion.

findings.issue: The test logs the exit code and every One action only / Outside band / Style check line as well as the TAG line the spec asked for.
findings.evidence: Lines 22-27: console.log(`exit ${code}`) and a filtered-lines log.
findings.fix: Optional: keep only console.log(tagLine). The extra logs help explain the known exit 1, so leaving them in is also fine.

summary: All SPEC items are implemented as the spec says, apart from the recorded Q-2 deviation for SPEC-02 (it asserts the band claim instead of exit 0). Changes: one band constant, the requirements text and change-log row, two locked band/postflop test edits within their approved scope (no assertion removed; the new oracle and the two non-vacuity counts match section 5 word for word), the opt-in slow test listed in test:slow, and docs. The fast tests for the changed files pass locally (6/6). The build log records the SPEC-05 mutation and SPEC-06 byte-identity results. There are no changes under src/bots, src/advice or src/engine. The doit/TASK-6.16/6.17/6.25/7.37 state.json diffs are orchestrator unlock bookkeeping. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
